newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Moore back in NZ Labour fold in bid to stop Nats.
newsitem.headline: Moore back in NZ Labour fold in bid to stop Nats.

text.p: Former Labour Party leader Mike Moore on Thursday said he had finally agreed to accept a positions on Labour's front bench because of the prospect of a National-led centre-right government.

"I think we could become a nasty little country if we have an indifferent, lazy National government that believes in nothing, that will compromise everything, clinging to office because of the Christian Party's social policy and ACT's economic policies," Moore told Radio New Zealand.
Moore, deposed by Helen Clark after the 1993 election, on Wednesday accepted an offer to be Labour's spokesman on foreign affairs and trade.
He had previously refused to take a prominent role in the party and earlier this year was rumoured to be planning to launch his own political party.

His decision to come in from the political wilderness came just hours after New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said he would offer Moore a cabinet post after the election, even if Labour was in opposition.
Moore said he could not rule out accepting a cabinet position in a NZ First-led government, but it would be at the behest of the Labour caucus.

"I'm not the leader and I'm not the caucus. If the caucus decision was (that) we will do work in colaition with New Zealand First or we will negotiate with the Alliance, obviously I would like to be part of that," he told the radio station.
He said he would not defect to the National Party under any circumstances.
Asked if the Labour leadership was in question as far as he was concerned, Moore replied: "Well I don't believe so, no."

He said he was confident Labour would be in a position to lead a centre-left government after the October 12 election and predicted the party would garner between 25 and 30 percent of the vote at the election.

"Let's try to form a new government with the majority dominated by solid, sensible, traditional Labour values that wants business to succeed so you can help the workers," Moore said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
